descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT TC-01 ER; TFA-92579 AC 3 · “Each patient renders as a card on the home screen showing: first and last name, room, chief diagnosis”.

Bug B23 · S1 · known

Patient cards are missing fields: age shows '76y' not '76F', Hospital cards have no hospital day, Nursing Home cards no visit number

Tickets: TFA-92579 AC3–4 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: dev + local

Note: Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579): the backend stores sex = F, yet the card shows '76y'; the Nursing Home diagnosis cells of TC-01/S03 and S26 are B28's root cause, so they need no Q4.

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S03, TC-01/S05, TC-01/S06, TC-01/S07

Approach · TC-01 Patient Chart Card · S26 Every card on a multi-patient list shows its own values, not a neighbour's (card-scoped)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U1 Each patient renders as a card on the home screen showing the patient's first and last name and room (Nursing Home: unit/room). (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U2 The card shows the chief diagnosis on Hospital cards only; a Nursing Home card shows no diagnosis. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3; UAT TC-03)
  • U3 The card shows age/sex in the "76F" format. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U4 The card shows the New Admission / Follow-up / Consult badge. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U5 The card shows the hospital day (Hospital) or the visit number (Nursing Home). (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U8 With multiple patients loaded, everything above holds in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-01; UAT 3.3)

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given seededCensus H1–H3 and N1, N3, N4 with pairwise-distinct values, plus a make-session-shaped Hospital patient (age 72, no sex) and resident (no unit); lists unfiltered

When On the unfiltered Hospital list and on both Nursing Home lists, scope to each card with page.getByRole('button', { name: `Open chart for ${name}` })

Then Each card contains its own room/unit, age/sex, badge, day/visit number (and diagnosis on Hospital only) and none of its neighbours' values; no invented sex or room

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Per card: toContainText(own values) and not.toContainText(each neighbour's values); NH cards not.toContainText(their stored diagnosis) (U2 / Q4). 3.4 identity line: the age-72 no-sex Hospital card not.toMatch(/\b72\s*y?\s*[FM]\b|\b(fe)?male\b/i); the unit-less resident card not.toMatch(/Room|Unit/i); no 'undefined' / 'null' / 'NaNy'. Day/visit format per Q2/Q3; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S26 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92579 ready for qa; TFA-92581 ready for qa

On a mixed list each card shows its own name, room and badge with nothing borrowed from a neighbour, but no card shows a hospital day or visit number, age reads '76y' without sex, and Nursing Home cards show the stored diagnosis.

Evidence: newspec-a, card-scoped. Missing day/visit = dev report §2 #5 (14 readings). Sex is Q1-dependent: there is no sex input anywhere in src/ (11 cells). The NH diagnosis = §2 #4 / Q4 (10 cells). Nothing leaks between cards, and no undefined/null/NaN appears.

Folded in: local datasets TC-01/S26 (same failure, folded into this result)

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.
